abstract: At each odd state of an actual Collatz trajectory, we measure the divisor supported at valuation levels present in the preceding L odd states. We bound the total logarithmic reuse by the actual division cost. On the final logarithmic-length window ending at the first crossing of height X from an entrance below X^theta, for fixed 0<theta<1, only O(L squared) tested positions can inherit a fixed positive fraction of their logarithmic height from this inventory. The exceptional proportion vanishes for lookback little-o of the square root of log X. A refined finite inequality has excess-division coefficient L(L−1)/2. We construct actual native trajectories proving this coefficient sharp for fixed L; these descending witnesses do not establish sharpness on recovery windows. If the prime support of the reused factors is bounded on specified blocks, a harmonic bound replaces the quadratic cost. We also give a least-cycle consequence and attach the first-crossing estimate to supplied subpolynomial-time precise returns. The proofs build on attributed prime-power return divisibility. No new cycle exclusion or precise-return existence claim is made.
